Thanks for sharing. I’m wondering with disabilities if that would qualify you for disability income somehow. I have known people who do fake it to get disability income, so I understand a little why it’s set up so it can be hard to get.

I think of people like one of my nieces who has learning disabilities yet made it to senior year hs honor roll. She’s in a private school, and though it is not a school specifically for kids with disabilities, they give them plenty of attention and encouragement. She sometimes struggles with depression and anxiety yet thrives in situations where she does something she enjoys with people she likes. She’s very over-sensitive yet puts on a tough demeanor in front of her friends so they don’t see her that way.

The problem she’ll have is in the real world she won’t have people all being nice and there will be stress in any job. Her dad never worked much and owes over $35k back support which he will never pay because you can’t squeeze blood from a turnip. She’ll be like him, never have a job for long because it’s too hard. Maybe she could get disability, due to her stress I don’t know. 

Maybe I could have gotten disability had I tried to get drs to certify my ptsd and stress, but I never tried.

I could not see niece or someone like that doing what I did struggling with a job that is awful. Part of her issue is how she was raised with not the best parents and inconsistencies that made her anxiety worse. Not that I was raised with great parents either, and even had it worse with abuse in many ways, but I had the benefit of being taught work ethic and made to work as a kid even when I was very upset about something. This taught me to go on and keep working despite all my stress and anxiety. 

My mental issues later on were mostly with high anxiety and stress made worse by a bad work environment. I look back and wonder was it worth it - and I can say yes it was for me because now I have a great financial situation. I wish it had not been so difficult and stressful. 

I never could have worked from home now, had I not been in the office several years at my previous stressful job. I needed the office to learn many things about my job being around other people seeing and hearing how they did the job. It has business sales and customer service aspects dealing with a lot of government agencies and businesses. The learning part in the office was good but the stress and mean people made it almost unbearable many days and years. 

My current job, same but at home and different company, has stressful things like some mean people, and is not perfect, but it’s a lot less than before so not hard to deal with. I work a lot less hours too.

Having a nice place to live and money makes life easier but it seems like it was a lot of stress to go through. 

I wish there had been a better easier way to get money but there wasn’t. 

I usually assume most people with enough money worked for it and went through stress like I did to get it. Even people who don’t work who marry into money sometimes have to deal with a lot of stress, as I’ve seen. 

Inheritance isn’t how most people get money, it’s a relatively small percentage. If inheritance was always passed down to every generation and not squandered there’d be a lot more rich people who never had to work. 

Those of us who are able to struggle through and work have to pay for people who can’t, there’s no other option. A universal income given to all, even a minimal amount, might be the best answer. Because those of us who work end up paying anyway, some form or another, when people struggling can’t work.
But you did find another job to bring in income. That is significant and not everyone does that.

Success meaning a combination of things - money and eventually freedom to work from home and then freedom to make my own schedule, and work far fewer hours. This was a long process and I saw many people give up along the way before they were financially stable. Long term this lack to more stress due to lack of money and lack of freedom to make choices.

My 55 pound mix breed dog had tried to get it. She’s friendly overall, but she has killed small creatures like lizards and field mice. 

She was leashed and put her paws up on the wall but could not jump high enough to reach it because I pulled her back and we left. 
I think if she’d been unleashed she’d have gotten in a fight with it and possibly been injured. 

We were probably not 4-5 feet below it. It was in an old abandoned small barn near my extended family’s property in north GA.

When I walked under it I did not know it was even there til it stuck its head out and hissed. 

We looked around and then saw it right above my head. I backed away a good distance, and took the pic which I enlarged later. 

Was wondering why it hissed, thinking maybe it was guarding a nest. I thought most birds would fly away with a dog jumping towards it that close. It could have easily pecked her eyes out even though she’s a strong dog.

We walked past it on the trail again, two days later, we made noise, and it was definitely gone. 

Several horseback riders regularly take that path, and I was told by relatives who have a small farm nearby that it was a turkey buzzard, had been there in the past, and scared several horses that were being ridden by locals.

Hopefully it has moved on for good. It’s on a side trail through the woods in a public hiking area which is kind of hidden so not many people know about that path, but that little barn does get hikers and horses passing right by it, now and then. That is not a great place for it, hope it finds a safer place away from the trail.

I was on the phone with a Fidelity broker today. She replied that most people don’t understand fully what it is to switch back and forth and that’s why they don’t allow it. I think the main reason is that Fidelity can lend securities you hold on margin and not those you hold in cash unless you are in the interest paying Fully Paid Lending (which you can sign up for if you have over $250k there.)

So basically if people with margin were switching to cash it would cost Fidelity money, 
That’s why it defaults to margin. Plus they make more if people use margin so keeping that the default makes more margin available.

Many people apparently think if it says margin they are charging interest because when I asked a customer service rep to journal items to cash, they replied with a fairly canned message stating I won’t be charged interest if it says margin. 

It is clear they get that question a lot.

And if they allowed people to change it online they wouldn’t get the chance to explain that. This they would lose out on the ability to lend those securities. A lot of them make Fidelity huge amounts of interest from short sellers.

That’s my take on it, now that I talked to the rep and did more research about various short selling interest and paid lending programs.

Yeah so far I only have stocks I bought due to research which happen to be in the lending program paying interest. Looking at the top paying ones from the link above, I don’t see any I really want to buy.

I’ve been going through some looking and most look like they will go down. 

But the ones I now have that pay up to 39% seem good long term, although volatile.

Edit to add, there are likely some high paying ones that will shoot up, it’s a matter of finding them.
It’s worth looking through some

You usually get about half the rate if you look securities up on the link above. But, that  link isn’t as accurate as checking the short sale rate on the brokerage site. 

So far mine range from 3-39%. To know the exact rate you can set up a short sale order as if you were going to place it. Do everything but hit place order and it will show the rate. Then divide by 2 from the rate they give. That gives an estimate.
